- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Model tends to overshoot in the middle of the 30-day horizon, particularly after a spike; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for days 10–20.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; increase forecast by 1–4% for last 5 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after high prices, then undercorrects after low prices; adjust for lagged momentum by adding 1–3% to forecasts following a 5%+ price drop.
- Model fails to capture long-term trend persistence; if history shows sustained upward trend, increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if history shows volatility > 2% per day.
- Model overestimates price stability after a spike; if forecast shows >10% spike followed by flatness, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
